turn_text: The water issue is one of those of too much or not enough. Your state has certainly felt that. The western part of the country has certainly felt that. The question is, is this a problem that seeks a national solution, a state solution, or will the answer come from a shared responsibility?

Well, I think it's a shared responsibility. With climate change having greater impacts, not only in our country, but around the world. I believe that water, water in the next 10 to 20 years around the world will rival energy as to whether or not nation states can live together amicably when certain regions of the world no longer find themselves with sufficient water to feed themselves. And by the way, we say in California where water flows, food grows. So when I'm saying feed themselves, you know, you can't grow any food without an adequate supply of water, then it must be addressed. And with 7 billion people plus on the planet, by the middle of the century over, they have 9 billion, water security in the United States, in California, and around the world will continue to be a crucible like energy as to whether or not we can have sustainability in the planet in the 21st century. Climate change is real. and it's impacting water availability in California in the United States and around the world. Therefore, we need to use all the water tools in our water toolbox. We provided additional funding in the last Congress with the Bureau of Reclamation, additional funding with the Department of Army Corps of Engineers, and the State of California has made its own efforts to try to create greater water reliability for our agricultural needs as well as for the rest of the challenges that we face in California as it relates to sustainability of our food production. We are trying to do a better job in groundwater recharge. We're focusing as one of our water management tools, improving our existing water supply facilities by expanding reservoirs improving our transfer systems in our canals, practicing greater water efficiency to ensure that we balance our overdraft challenges, and on coastal communities where it's applicable, desalination plays a role as well.
